findings.title: College scholarships and financial-aid pages give two different PCE scholarship deadlines (February 1 and February 8)

pages.says: Confirmed live today. Deadline list: "February 1st - PCE General Scholarships application deadline for current and incoming students." Older tabs on the same page: "Set a deadline at least 1-2 weeks before the February 8th application deadline"; "References are due February 7th"; David Jorgensen Scholarship "Opens: December 1 Closes: February 8"; "A current student who submits a John and Marcia Price College of Engineering scholarship application by February 8th will automatically be considered for department and college level awards."

Confirmed live today: "February 8 – Scholarship deadline for John and Marcia Price College of Engineering scholarships". The same page (saved copy) also says: "For incoming freshmen, the scholarship application deadline is February 1st during their senior year of high school".

findings.official_says: Admissions lists "December 1" as the freshman "Merit Scholarship Consideration Deadline" and "February 1" as the "Financial Aid Priority Date". The PCE General Scholarships deadline is the college's own date, so PCE Student Services has to say which one is right. The page's newest sections, and the FAFSA date, both say February 1.
findings.why_it_matters: A student who goes by the February 8 date (the David Jorgensen Scholarship, the current-student tab, the reference instructions, or the Financial Aid page) could submit after a February 1 deadline and lose consideration for up to 290 college and department scholarships. The 2027 cycle opens December 1, about six weeks from now.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the 2027 deadline. Then delete the older duplicate tabs on /scholarships (the Incoming First-Year, Transfer and Current Student tabs and the old Application Instructions that say February 8/February 7). Make the Jorgensen close date and the reference due date match, and change the Financial Aid page's 'Dates to Remember' to the same date.
findings.owner: PCE Student Services (scholarships), with the college web team

verdict.reason: Live today, /scholarships has the deadline list saying "February 1st - PCE General Scholarships application deadline for current and incoming students." The same page still says Jorgensen "Closes: February 8", "Set a deadline at least 1-2 weeks before the February 8th application deadline", "References are due February 7th" and, in the old Transfer tab, "by February 8th". /financial-aid still says "February 8 – Scholarship deadline for John and Marcia Price College of Engineering scholarships" and, on the same page, "February 1st" for incoming freshmen.

findings.title: GRE described as both optional and required (with minimum scores) on ChemE, Mechanical and MSE graduate admissions pages and handbooks

pages.says: Confirmed live today: "The GRE is no longer required for PhD or MS admissions to the Department of Chemical Engineering." and "GRE scores are optional for all PhD and MS applicants."

The 'Graduate Handbook' link on the page above opens this file (checked live today): "GRE scores are required from all applicants, regardless of background or previous degrees. The minimum GRE score ... is 155 for master's applicants and 160 for PhD applicants"
Confirmed live today: "In a normal year, we require a score of 80th percentile or higher on the GRE Quantitative section ... the GRE exam is optional for 2021 and 2022 admission"

Confirmed live today: "The GRE is optional", yet the same page says the application is not complete "until the online application is submitted and the Admissions Office has received your official GRE test scores and application fee."

Confirmed live today: "GRE Score (Not required, but highly recommended by department)" and also "The Department requires applicants GRE score to be a minimum combined score of 300 on the quantitative and verbal sections; and a minimum score of 3.0 on the writing section."
Checked live today: GRE scores "are not required, but highly recommended. There is no minimum score requirement"

findings.official_says: The Graduate School sets no GRE requirement: "Each graduate program sets its own application deadlines and requirements." Its minimum is "A 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA in the undergraduate career". Each department's own current policy decides, so each department has to pick one.
findings.why_it_matters: Applicants for Fall 2027 (ChemE priority deadlines in December and January, Mechanical on January 1, MSE on January 15) may pay for and schedule a GRE they don't need. Others may decide not to apply because they think they fall below a 155/160, 80th-percentile or 300 minimum that the department's main page says doesn't exist.
findings.suggested_fix: ChemE: update the GRE section of the 2026-27 Graduate Handbook to match the website (optional). Mechanical: rewrite the FAQ answer 'Is the GRE Exam Required?' and the retake/low-score answers, and remove 'official GRE test scores' from the completeness note on the deadlines page. MSE: delete the 300/3.0 minimum sentence, or state it as a recommendation, so it matches the handbook.
findings.owner: Graduate admissions/advising in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Materials Science & Engineering

verdict.reason: Every quote checked out live. The ChemE page says "The GRE is no longer required", but the 2026-27 handbook PDF it links (ModDate 2026-08-24) says "GRE scores are required from all applicants... 155 for master's applicants and 160 for PhD applicants". The Mech FAQ still has the 80th-percentile rule with "optional for 2021 and 2022". The Mech deadlines page says "The GRE is optional" but also that an application is not complete until Admissions "has received your official GRE test scores". MSE admissions says "Not required, but highly recommended" and also "The Department requires... a minimum combined score of 300", while the MSE handbook says "There is no minimum score requirement".
